title: Dev app run file
description: What the iOS and Android dev apps load and how they run it, passed whole as the --run argument (iOS) or the run extra (Android). Without one, the app opens the default world for interactive use.

file.description: An absolute path, or a name in the app's Documents (iOS, then the bundle) or external files dir (Android). A .json file streams a tiled world.

source_frame.description: The frame the world and collider were written in, one letter for each of rl, ud and bf, such as rdf; defaults to the format's own frame.

collider.description: A collider GLB, found like file.

renderer.description: The quality level first, then each field given here.

quality.description: iOS takes ultra, high, balanced or fast; Android takes ultra, high, medium or low. Defaults to high.

budget.description: Splats a hierarchy world loads, 0 for the device default.

subpixel.description: Footprint in pixels under which a splat is not drawn.

lod_error_pixels.description: Screen error a hierarchy node may cover before it splits.

lod_splat_limit.description: Most splats a frame selects, 0 for the loaded budget.

pose.description: Starting camera x, y, z in metres, then yaw and pitch in radians.

run.description: A scripted run: HUD hidden, screen kept awake, touch and gyroscope off. Without orbit the camera turns once in place and logs the frame time distribution.

seconds.description: Length of the turn or the orbit.

orbit.description: iOS only: orbits anchor from pose after the first frame, then stops the run.

capture_at.description: iOS only: seconds after the first frame to write Documents/capture.png.

monitor.description: iOS only: logs footprint, Metal allocation and thermal state at 2 Hz and stops the run on memory or thermal pressure.
